Cinematic key art for a prestige driving game, 16:9 widescreen. A wide establishing shot of an independent used-car lot in Houston, Texas, late at night after close, seen from a low camera at knee height standing at the far left edge of the lot. The horizon sits at about 45 percent of the frame height. Three long rows of clean late-model sedans, pickups and SUVs, small in the frame (each car no wider than about a tenth of the frame), parked in neat rows that recede diagonally away to the right, all seen from behind: rear quarters, tail lights and roof lines only, tail lights dark, never grilles, front badges or license plates. Sodium-vapor pole lights stand among the rows and recede in perspective into the distance, each lamp head small and warm, casting soft amber pools on the roofs. Far back on the right, a modest single-story showroom with plain glass windows lit warm from inside, small in the frame, no lettering on it. The asphalt is wet from rain and holds long vertical sodium reflections. Low palm silhouettes and power lines along the horizon against a humid sky that is dark green-black with faint haze. Composition: the lot, cars, poles and showroom all sit in the right 60 percent of the frame; the left 40 percent falls to near-black empty wet ground and dark sky, calm and deep, for type. The top 18 percent of the right half is plain dark sky with no lamp, no pole head and no bright light in it; every lamp head sits lower than that. Palette: bottle green shadows (#1C3229 into near-black #0A0F0D), warm sodium amber practical light, bone white highlights (#EDE7DB). Photographic, quiet, after-hours, 35mm anamorphic feel, deep focus, fine film grain, painterly restraint. Absolutely no people, no readable text, no signage, no letters, no logos, no brand emblems or badges, no license plates, no neon, no lens flares, no bloom, no plastic CGI gloss. (model gpt-image-2.5-sunburst via Figma)
The second pole light from the left (its head, glow, pole and its reflection on the wet ground) was removed in code before grading, so no lamp sits behind the tile labels: tools/art/candidates/triple-j-w1r.py fitted the sky around it and kept the fine grain, filled the pole row by row, then rebuilt the ground under it from the car base down from the asphalt either side, keeping the asphalt's ripples at the ground's level, with matched grain.
